newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut takes breather as market seeks direction.
newsitem.headline: Beirut takes breather as market seeks direction.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange took a breather in the week ended on Friday and brokers said the market was searching for direction ahead of mid-year bank results.
Weekly turnover fell to 710,563 shares from 1,135,002 and value dropped to $6,376,190 from $8,856,314.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.37 percent to 153.78. The LISPI general index fell 0.41 percent to 89.42 and the BLOM general index fell 0.94 percent to 932.14.
"It was a quiet week. It is the right time to come in as prices are just taking a breather," said one broker, who asked not to be identified.
Of the three bank shares, Bank Audi hit a new high of $23.25 after last week's record $23.125. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell to $18 from $18.5 and Bank of Beirut ended unchanged at $3.937.
"BOB and BLC are trading within a narrow range between resistance and support, indicating the market was waiting for mid-year results in search of direction," the broker said.
Solidere shares fell in heavy demand and brokers said mis-matching between supply and demand was the cause of the relatively small number traded on the week.
A shares fell to $10.5 from $10.625 and B shares fell to $10.75 from $10.875.
"Solidere shares are a very good buy," the broker said. "Investors are interested. They are rushing in before the share goes ex-dividend. This in turn has contracted supply."
Total weekly supply of Solidere on the first daily fixing was 903,450 shares against demand of over two million. Turnover on both daily fixings was 284,488 shares.
Of the four industrial shares, Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125 and Eternit was unchanged at $2.
There was no trade in the other two listed firms, Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
